root.name: Philidor Defense: Nimzowitsch, Locock Variation
root.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 d6 3. d4 Nf6 4. Ng5

overview: In the Nimzowitsch Philidor White tries 4.Ng5, aiming at f7 in the Locock style. The knight sac on f7 gives White a couple of pawns and a king in the open for Black, but with correct play Black comes out ahead. Black can also meet 4.Ng5 with ...d5 or ...Qe7 and a quiet game.

white_ideas.idea: Sacrifice Nxf7 for pawns and an exposed king
Break open the centre with dxe5 and Bc4+

black_ideas.idea: Meet the knight with ...d5 and develop

typical_structures.structure: White knight on g5 and Black f7 pawn under attack

character.notes: Tricky tactics with White hoping for a quick attack against the Black king.

gambit.notes: In the Locock line Black takes the knight on f7 and can keep the extra piece.

sublines_that_differ.name: Locock Variation
sublines_that_differ.how: White gives the knight for two pawns.

character.reason: White tries a sacrifice on f7 and a mistake by either side decides quickly.

gambit.reason: The Locock line gives a knight for pawns that Black can keep.

soundness.reason: The sacrifice is thought to be unsound against correct defence.

structure.reason: Pieces and open lines after exchanges in the centre.
